# Funnel lab

Open `/lab/` for the experimental workshop. The original kit page and core renderer remain unchanged.

The workshop UI is written as React components in `src/lab/` and built to `dist/lab/lab.js` by `npm run build:lab`. `npm run dev` watches the source. `Figure.tsx` owns the boundary to the existing SVG renderer; controls, data editing, comparison, and saved configurations use React state. Edit the source files rather than the generated bundle. `verify-lab-ui.mjs` checks the mounted workshop and particle study.

The floating DialKit panel controls the transition between Vertical prisms. A direct pointer switch lets the previous prism settle into the stack while the next expands, using the same geometry as ordinary proximity inspection. Crossfade fades the old and new focus together, Overlap lets the new focus appear before the old one leaves, and Relay fades the old focus out before the next enters. The Animations switch makes the handoff immediate while retaining proximity expansion. Playback Speed ranges from 0.1× to 4×; at 1× the crossfade lasts 150 ms. These choices persist in this browser. The panel affects the lab preview only, while the React package defaults to Crossfade at 150 ms. `npm run build:lab` also generates `dist/lab/dialkit.css` from the installed DialKit styles.

`default-configs.js` holds three independent presets. Page load and Reset variant restore that variant's complete preset, including data and print settings. The older branching export is migrated to the connected bucket tree, preserving its print settings and aggregate quantities. New sample keeps the active print settings while regenerating data.

Vertical samples keep the final quantity at least 10% of the first, so repeated random losses do not make the last prism a hairline. The isometric renderer also reserves visible height for every front face when losses are uneven; front widths still represent the actual quantities. The default preset and imported values are not rewritten.

Each variant has independent settings. On desktop, the controls sidebar scrolls independently of the figure. Shared controls adjust the chart pattern, screen pitch, hatch angle, outline weight (0.25–0.75 pt), dot gain (−80% to +20%), edge irregularity, label size, annotations, and optional paper grain. The lab uses only blue ink (`#2F4FE0`) and cool gray paper (`#E4E5E8`). Each individual pattern fills every ribbon in that variant. Atlas mix is the default for all three variants. It distributes the five available patterns across ribbons, keeping neighboring branches distinct where possible. Available patterns are dense stochastic stipple, 30% AM dots, diagonal hatch, 50% diamond lattice, and 70% coarse dots. Stipple is seeded across the entire figure rather than repeated from a small tile. Dense stipple has over twice the previous dot count; reducing dot gain makes dots smaller without reducing their number. A WebGL 2 point shader generates the seeded dots without building per-dot DOM or path commands. It keeps the full-figure distribution, six dot sizes, and independent dot-gain control. WebGL-unavailable browsers use the original six grouped vector paths. Solid ink is reserved for small marks. Older sparse stipple configurations load as dense stipple; older Atlas mix configurations retain the mix. All labels are English. Vertical is the first and default lab figure. Continuous funnels offer Half and Full mirror shapes; the mirrored form uses the same chart area, with full symmetric thickness encoding quantity. Both shapes expose curvature, height, and an optional eased fade over 0–45% of the first ribbon's left edge and last ribbon's right edge; intermediate ribbons remain fully visible. Vertical funnels open in isometric view and offer a Flat view switch. Each Vertical view remembers its own print and geometry controls, including height, stage gaps, border radius (0–20 px), and terminal taper. The dataset and seed remain common to both views. Flat view also exposes cap curvature; its widths decrease with quantity, and adjacent rims share the same visible span even when corners are rounded. Isometric view keeps front widths proportional to stage quantities, with sparse stipple on top and screened side faces for depth. Projection depth is adjustable from 18–200 px; the canvas expands to keep deeper tops, sides, and labels visible. Rotating across zero reveals the opposite side while every stage follows the same tapered prism. Branching funnels expose curvature, branch spacing, and node width. The branching variant is one connected bucket tree. Each child has exactly one parent, and every non-final bucket distributes 100% of its quantity to its children, including any drop-off bucket. Node widths and adjoining ribbon widths use one common quantity scale. An optional `value` on a node asserts its quantity, including the entry total; mismatches with links are rejected. Shared destinations, multiple entry buckets, and incomplete splits are rejected with an explanation; the renderer never duplicates a bucket or resumes a disconnected aggregate. The diagram grows vertically when necessary instead of squeezing lanes together; deep graphs gain horizontal space and remain scrollable.

`config.js` generates deterministic examples and validates portable configurations. Version 3 configurations contain their version, variant, seed, all options, and complete data. Vertical configurations also store separate `verticalViews.flat` and `verticalViews.isometric` control sets; older configurations initialize both sets from their existing options when imported, with a valid Isometric taper for an untapered Flat preset. Version 1 imports retain the screen migration; old opacity settings are discarded. Existing isometric configurations migrate into Vertical with isometric view selected. Older Vertical configurations without a view setting retain the flat view. Seed-generated branching examples from versions 1 and 2 regenerate as connected trees while retaining their seed and print settings. Synthetic channel activation counts are allocated within the example generator; imported custom data is never apportioned or rewritten. `lab-engine.js` renders those options without mutating the original library. New sample assigns a new seed; changing a seed regenerates its data. Applying JSON data marks the configuration as custom.

Save configuration retains a named copy in browser storage. Select it from the shelf to restore it. Export config downloads the full JSON; Import config restores that JSON with validation. Export SVG includes every ribbon, even when a path is pinned, and excludes interaction overlays. The shader screens are embedded as 3× PNGs in the SVG; the lab preview uses 2× screens. Other geometry remains vector. Mouse hover settles a thin contour over the selected section and its connected path in 150 ms; leaving takes 110 ms. A nearby pointer draws the contour along the funnel's flow direction—horizontally for continuous and branching, vertically for either Vertical view—and the contour settles onto the section on contact. The filled geometry stays stationary. Keyboard and touch feedback is immediate, and reduced-motion preferences disable all transitions and proximity movement.

The new React package entry uses this renderer and accepts the lab geometry options. The original kit page and its legacy React adapter still use the older renderer. To render a lab config programmatically in the browser:

```js
import { renderFunnel } from './lab-engine.js';
import { parseConfig } from './config.js';
const config = parseConfig(savedJson);
const svg = renderFunnel(config.data, {
  ...config.options,
  variant: config.variant,
  seed: config.seed,
  idPrefix: 'my-figure',
});
document.querySelector('#figure').replaceChildren(svg);
```

Open `/lab/benchmark.html` to compare the shader and original vector field on the same seeded figure. It reports median cold build and first-frame times over three seeds, warm reuse, dot count, and serialized SVG size, with side-by-side previews. Serve `dist/` over HTTP for development. From the repository root run `node verify-lab.mjs` to check deterministic sampling, configuration round trips, validation, and geometry at slider limits.

## Idle motion prototype

Open `/lab/idle-motion/` to tune idle motion for the isometric Vertical prism. It combines a floating island drift with data flowing between stages, and the main lab links to it. The page renders the default Vertical preset through `AtlasFunnel`. Its React source is `src/lab/idle-motion/main.tsx`, and `npm run build:lab` generates `idle.js`.

Each stage drifts through the CSS `translate` property, so the drift composes with the proximity `transform` without replacing it. Island controls set lift (0–16 px), side shift (0–24 px), cycle length (1–20 s), and stagger between stages (0–4 s). Dots leave the hidden bottom face of one stage and land at the same depth on the next stage's top face, clipped below the source stage's front edge. Flow controls set fall time (120–3000 ms), dot rate at the widest gap (0–60 per second, scaled down by stage quantity), and dot radius (0.3–3 px). Corner hatch shades each front face's lower-right corner with hand-drawn strokes at the preset's hatch angle. Each stroke appears at a random point near the corner, draws in, holds, and erases. Positions are weighted toward the corner and strokes shorten with distance, so the corner stays darkest while the shading keeps changing. Controls set strokes per corner on the top stage (0–120), reach (6–120 px), stroke weight (0.2–2 px), draw time (60–3000 ms), hold (0–12 s, randomized ±50%), and erase time (60–3000 ms). Lower stages scale stroke count and reach by front-face height. Directions (1–4) adds hatch angles that step from the screen angle by angle step (5–90°), and jitter (0–30°) tilts each stroke at random. Layered mix allows each further direction only closer to the corner, building cross-hatched tone. Mixed lets any direction appear anywhere. Mark style chooses Halftone, Match screen, or Lines. Halftone, the default, inks dots on the AM screen's grid on every face, growing toward the corner like a halftone gradient, at halftone density (1–8× the stroke count). Halftone dot size (0.3–4 px, default 1.55 px) sets the largest radius reached at the corner, and other halftone marks scale with it. Dots larger than half the 3 px grid pitch merge into solid ink. Dots smaller than the AM screen's own 1.1 px dots no longer darken that face. The AM face swells its own dots, and the closed coarse halftone inks its gaps. Lines uses hatch strokes everywhere. With Match screen, each face's marks follow its screen, read from the face's pattern fill. Stipple faces get small stipple dots, at stipple density (1–12× the stroke count) and stipple size (0.2–1.5 px radius). Open halftones swell their real grid dots toward touching. Closed halftones, whose dots already overlap, ink the paper gaps at cell corners. Cross screens hatch at the screen angle and 90° from it. Hatch screens use the direction controls. Side face lets the shading continue around the same corner onto the side face. With Yield to hover on, all three motions settle while a stage is inspected, pinned, or focused, then resume. Reduced motion disables both. The DialKit panel persists in this browser, and Reset restores the defaults. The main lab plays the same motion on the Vertical figure in isometric view, with the same Idle motion panel. Both pages store values under one id, so tuning carries between them. Flat view and the other variants have no idle motion. `src/lab/idle-motion/motion.ts` holds the shared hook, the panel, and `stripIdleMotion()`. Export SVG uses `stripIdleMotion()` so exported figures are still and contain no motion layers. The React package does not include idle motion.
